Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026

claims.text: RTX supplies commercial aerospace systems, aircraft engines and defense technologies. It combines aircraft production and aftermarket exposure with government procurement.
The three segments are Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon. Revenue includes equipment sales, parts, repairs, engine support and defense contracts.
Examples include Collins aircraft systems, Pratt & Whitney GTF and F135 engines, and Raytheon Patriot, AMRAAM and radar systems.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Business Segments / Collins Aerospace; Pratt & Whitney; Raytheon

claims.text: Customers include airframe manufacturers, aircraft operators, U.S. government agencies and international buyers. Commercial aviation and defense create distinct demand drivers.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Business Segments; Sales and Customers

claims.text: Original engine and aircraft-system placements create later service opportunities. Supplier reliability, overhaul capacity and regulatory approval affect delivery and service economics.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Competition; Item 1A, suppliers and product quality

claims.text: The filing describes competition in aircraft equipment, spares and defense systems. Defense suppliers may also be partners or competitors on different programs.
Interpretation: installed engines and certified systems can support aftermarket durability. Alternative parts suppliers, pricing competition and maintenance obligations limit the advantage.
The July results reported commercial aftermarket and defense growth. Management plans capacity and productivity improvements; future backlog conversion still depends on execution.
For April 1–June 30, 2026, GAAP sales were USD 24,708 million, net income attributable to common shareowners USD 2,139 million and diluted EPS USD 1.57.
Adjusted diluted EPS was USD 1.89 for that quarter. This company-defined non-GAAP measure excludes acquisition accounting and specified restructuring and other items.
At June 30, 2026, GAAP cash and equivalents were USD 8,305 million. GAAP long-term debt was USD 31,858 million, excluding USD 5,296 million of current maturities and other short-term borrowings.
The July results identify Chris Calio as chairman and CEO. The September succession filing names Jill Albertelli as Pratt & Whitney’s future president.

evidence.locator: Item 5.02, Retirement of Named Executive Officer

claims.text: Interpretation: compare segment profitability and cash generation while reconciling acquisition adjustments and engine remediation costs. No current stock price, valuation multiple or price target is supplied.

claims.text: Announced September 15, 2026: Jill Albertelli is scheduled to succeed Shane Eddy as Pratt & Whitney president on January 1, 2027. Execution effects remain uncertain.

evidence.locator: Item 5.02, Retirement of Named Executive Officer

claims.text: Powder-metal issues require accelerated GTF inspections and additional shop visits. Costs depend on inspection findings, overhaul capacity and customer compensation; deteriorating estimates would weaken a cash-recovery thesis.

evidence.locator: Note 16, Pratt & Whitney Powder Metal Matter

claims.text: Interpretation: upside combines aftermarket growth with profitable defense deliveries; downside includes engine remediation, supply constraints or contract overruns. No scenario probabilities or target prices are assigned.

evidence.locator: Item 2, Business Overview; Note 16, Commitments and Contingencies

claims.text: Pratt & Whitney’s F135 powers Lockheed Martin’s F-35. This is a documented propulsion-platform relationship; shared defense exposure alone does not establish another customer relationship.
RTX raised its adjusted sales, adjusted EPS and free-cash-flow outlook on July 23, 2026. These were management forecasts, not realized annual results.

gaps: No current stock price, consensus estimates or valuation multiples were sourced.
Latest quarterly evidence covers June 30, 2026; filings-first pilot is not an exhaustive news or contract-award feed.
Full debt maturity, engine-remediation cash and litigation models are not built.
Named commercial aerospace competitors and market shares require separate primary-source comparison.
